# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States and has about 1,100 staff. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage.

The Client's AI portfolio has three use cases:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

**Drivers and constraints**

- **Regulation:** the EU AI Act and GDPR.
- **Certification target:** ISO/IEC 42001. Work is to start next year, and the start date is not fixed.
- **Audit finding:** an internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems.
- **Stated objective:** "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." (Dana Whitfield)
- **Budget:** approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- **Data:** customer data must stay in the EU.
- **Works council:** the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.
- **Decision:** a decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

This proposal sets out how the Guided AI GRC Build would take the Client from these starting facts to a functioning minimum viable Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) in twelve weeks.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement can deliver a finished set of documents. It can also leave the organization dependent on outside help to interpret, maintain and evidence those documents.

The Guided AI GRC Build works differently. The Client's own build team writes the charter, populates the inventory, runs the assessments, adopts the policies and starts the evidence cycles. Each week combines:

- one live virtual workshop;
- one coaching session; and
- structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.

The consultant's role is to provide method, review and challenge. The Client's role is to make the decisions and own the artifacts.

This matters for three reasons tied to the Client's position:

1. **The audit finding.** The June 2026 finding concerned the absence of an AI inventory. A remedy the Client's team has built and can operate is better placed to withstand follow-up review than one held by an outside party.
2. **The certification target.** ISO/IEC 42001 is a target, and an AIMS must be operated, reviewed and improved over time. A team that built the system can run it.
3. **The audience.** The build team includes the two internal auditors. The program proposes to involve them as participants throughout, so the people who will later test the system understand its design.

The program applies three principles throughout:

- **Slow AI holds that** AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.
- **Informed Intent:** no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions.
- **Final Liability rests with the Human:** every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene.

**Working frameworks**

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

**Board-layer reference:** AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards)

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory sequencing (proposed for Week 2)**

| Order | System | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Customer service chatbot | It is the only deployed use case. |
| 2 | AI visual inspection | It is in pilot, and the stated objective ties governance to its move into production in Q2 2027. |
| 3 | AI sales forecasting | It is recorded as a planned system, so governance can apply before it is built. |

**ISO/IEC 42001 readiness themes.** These are mapped below as readiness themes only. The program does not promise certification, audit or regulatory outcomes.

**Integration with incumbent frameworks.** The Client operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. The program will attach to existing structures rather than build parallel ones. However, an integration point is named only where a specific existing artifact is known. For the ISMS and the quality management system, integration points are Unknown until intake confirms which artifacts each holds.

| Week | Focus | Tailoring to the Client (proposed work) | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter scoped to the three use cases. Named owner per system assigned under Final Liability rests with the Human. Steering checkpoint 1. | Context, scope, leadership, roles | ISMS: Unknown. QMS: Unknown |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Inventory built in the order shown above. | Context, AI system records | Internal audit: June 2026 finding (no inventory of AI systems) |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | EU AI Act classification approach for each system, with GDPR touchpoints identified. Confirm with external counsel. | Planning, risk criteria | ISMS: Unknown |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Assessments for the chatbot and visual inspection first. Works council consultation triggers identified. Confirm with external counsel. | AI risk assessment, impact assessment | QMS: Unknown |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Operating register covering all three systems, with treatment owners named. | Risk treatment | ISMS: Unknown |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core policy set adopted, including an Informed Intent authorization standard. Steering checkpoint 2. | Policy, leadership commitment | ISMS: Unknown. QMS: Unknown |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Pilot-to-production gate defined for visual inspection. | Operational planning and control | QMS: Unknown |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection starts | Supplier requirements include the EU customer data constraint. Evidence collection begins. | Third-party relationships, documented information | ISMS: Unknown |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | At least two governed workflows brought into production use. The chatbot is a candidate. The second workflow is Unknown. | Operation, human oversight | QMS: Unknown |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring defined for each governed workflow. | Performance evaluation | ISMS: Unknown |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change routes defined. Four-week evidence check. | Nonconformity, improvement | ISMS: Unknown. QMS: Unknown |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Walkthrough with the two internal auditors participating. Steering checkpoint 3. | Internal audit readiness, management review | Internal audit: Unknown |

Items with legal effect, including AI Act classification, GDPR positions, works council consultation and contractual terms: confirm with external counsel.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The program contracts for a minimum viable AIMS consisting of all six of the following elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Second governed workflow.** Only one use case is currently deployed. The second governed workflow in production use is therefore Unknown and is the first item to confirm at intake.

**Relation to the Q2 2027 objective.** The program start date is Unknown. Whether Week 12 falls before the stated Q2 2027 production objective depends on when the program starts.

## 5. Client Team Commitment per Week

All figures below are estimates in hours. They cover the workshop, the coaching session and asynchronous work. Actual effort will vary with the Client's existing documentation.

| Role | Typical week (estimate) | Peak weeks (estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 | 5 in Weeks 1, 3, 6 and 12 |
| CISO | 3 | 5 in Weeks 8, 10 and 11 |
| Head of Quality | 3 | 5 in Weeks 7, 11 and 12 |
| Head of Data | 4 | 6 in Weeks 2, 9 and 10 |
| German plant manager | 2 | 4 in Weeks 2, 4 and 9 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 | 4 in Weeks 11 and 12 |

In a typical week, the team commitment totals an estimated 19 hours.

## 6. Steering Cadence

An executive steering checkpoint takes place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

| Week | Purpose |
|---|---|
| 1 | Confirms scope, team and decisions needed. |
| 6 | Reviews spine status, blockers and any scope decisions. |
| 12 | Receives the minimum viable AIMS attestation against the six elements, together with a 12-month operating plan. |

Board-layer reporting draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). Steering membership is Unknown and is to be confirmed at intake.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format:** all workshops and coaching sessions are virtual. Team locations and time zones are to be confirmed at intake so sessions can be scheduled.

**Price:** US$60,000 for the twelve-week program. This sits within the stated budget approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

**Commercial terms:** payment terms and the fiscal year dates are Unknown and are to be agreed at contracting. Contract terms: confirm with external counsel.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The proposed next step is a short intake session to confirm the following:

1. Steering membership and the named owner for each AI system.
2. Whether the chatbot processes customer data, and where that data is held.
3. Whether the visual inspection pilot touches production staff, and the timing of works council consultation.
4. The candidate for the second governed workflow in production use.
5. Which existing ISMS, quality management system and internal audit artifacts the program should attach to.
6. The intended start date for the program and for ISO/IEC 42001 work.

Once these are confirmed, the Week 1 mobilization brief can be issued and the program start date agreed.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: Checklist item 4 is recorded not applicable because Mode A has no weekly assignments. Another scorer could apply it to the spine table, which names no repository asset per week, and fail the case.

The Week 2 integration point 'Internal audit: June 2026 finding (no inventory of AI systems)' attaches to an artifact the Profile Block states under RISK_EVENTS. I treated it as permitted. A stricter scorer could read it as an inferred relation between the finding and the internal audit function.

'The Client operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function' restates INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS. I treated it as a fact the block gives, not an asserted register, process or control. ISMS and QMS integration points are correctly rendered Unknown.

'The build team includes the two internal auditors' follows from AUDIENCE_ROLES and is paired with proposed-work language ('The program proposes to involve them'). I treated it as a given fact, not an invented relation.
Section 3 states 'It is the only deployed use case' for the chatbot. I treated this as a direct reading of AI_USE_CASES.

The scorer guidance of v1.14.3 permits consequences of stated constraints and proposed work, such as the works council consultation triggers and the supplier requirement on EU customer data. I applied it to those items.
